The three regions tile one disk and do not overlay the housing. Hidden axle, teeth, switch mechanism and PCB are unmodeled.

Current coreink-d67 digital subset has actual LX6/production Worker evidence for SSD1681 display, GPIO37/38/39/5/27 keys and BM8563 calendar. This does not accept the old M09 command stream, LED/buzzer, main-power behavior, RTC alarm/wake, analog e-paper timing, complete factory firmware or physical hardware. See docs/platform/m5-classic-paper-runtime-20261126.md and docs/platform/evidence/m5-final-integration-20261126/classic-thirteen.json.
Photo and geometry comparisons remain partial; no complete 1:1 manufacturing or populated-PCB certification.
Source CAD MIT and manufacturer photographs have distinct rights; no separate open photo license verified.
Blank display rectangle uses documented active dimensions when available; placement/window boundary is estimated from photos/CAD, not a calibrated measurement.
The older promotional image labels50x40x16 while current specification and selected CAD are56x40x16; this mismatch is retained, not silently reconciled.

The missing visible black three-way dial is now a separate photo-estimated cap; only its three actual surface regions emit the catalog GPIO37/38/39 button inputs. The native enclosure triangles and photographic artifacts are unchanged. No mechanical encoder or hidden switch accuracy is claimed.

The existing native actuator face is selected by explicit original source-face ranges. The ordered original vertex/normal binary is unchanged; unmapped adjacent shell and reset areas remain ordinary occluders.
